module.title: Aqueous phase stability and Pourbaix thermodynamics
module.expensive_path: Composition-compatible multientry enumeration and reaction balancing, geometric halfspace construction, and batched pH/potential evaluation across stable phases. Entry count, component count and condition-grid size control cost; owned work versus SciPy/core dependency work must be profiled before the acceleration check is selected.
module.rationale: One scientific model and energy convention from aqueous/solid entries through stable domains to decomposition energies. Offline Zn and multicomponent upstream fixtures provide reference assertions without API credentials.
excluded: Materials Project API queries and newly downloaded databases
Solid-state PhaseDiagram and reaction balancing implementations now owned by pymatgen-core
hazards: Qhull joggling, degenerate phases and phase-boundary ties require physical equivalence rather than raw facet or vertex ordering
Keep entry identity and normalization conventions explicit; compare energy in eV/atom and stable phase identity where unique
Public upstream fixture provenance still needs a payload-specific source-PR review
The upstream multiprocessing test uses all host CPUs; initial native investigation excludes it and records that limitation
Twenty-one upstream test definitions include serialization and plotting; no final suitable-check count is claimed yet

approval.human_ref: Looks good. But can we add regular phase diagram utilities in pymatgen.analysis.phase_diagram as well?

shared_infrastructure: pymatgen-core==2026.8.30 supplies Structure, Lattice, Composition, slab generation, elasticity, reaction balancing and phase-diagram helpers; dependency, not owned implementation in this source snapshot
NumPy and SciPy numerical kernels; spglib symmetry; monty serialization
